name: Zero rule
summary: In the presence of the zero scalar, any wire can be cut.
description:
A Z-spider with phase π and no legs represents the scalar $1+e^{i\pi}=0$. In a diagram that contains this zero scalar, any wire can be replaced by a disconnected Z-effect and X-state, since both sides are then the zero map. Together with the [zero scalar rule](../zero-scalar-rule/) this allows bringing any zero diagram into a normal form that only depends on its numbers of inputs and outputs.

The rule was suggested by Kissinger and introduced as an axiom by Backens to make the stabilizer ZX-calculus complete for diagrams with scalars. In the simplified rule set of Backens, Perdrix and Wang it is replaced by the [state version](../zero-rule-state/).

source.location: Section 4.3 (Completeness for stabilizer zero diagrams), zero rule
